discovery: Controlled/living radical polymerization (transition-metal-catalyzed atom transfer radical polymerization, ATRP), which enables precise synthesis of polymers with defined architectures
rationale: ATRP is among the most cited and industrially used advances in synthetic chemistry. Since the mid-1990s it has made precision polymer synthesis routine, and its developers have won many major prizes that often come before a Nobel (Wolf Prize, Kyoto Prize). The 2024 prize went to protein design and structure prediction, and the 2025 prize to MOFs. That makes a return to classical synthetic and materials chemistry plausible, and polymer chemistry is due for recognition.
